parsed.explanation: The inference "|E|<|V| implies no cycle and no loop anywhere" is false: isolated vertices elsewhere can absorb the edge budget. Concrete instance (n=2, pieces 4u,2u,u): Y halves the u-piece and halves the 4u-piece, giving parts 2u,2u,2u,u/2,u/2; a tie-break can pair the two 2u parts of the top piece with each other, creating a loop at vertex n=2, while the edge {2u of piece 1, u/2 of piece 0} leaves |E|=2<|V|=3. So the component of vertex n need not be loop/cycle-free, and the proper 2-colouring step fails for it. The load-bearing claim appears only here. Repair: |E|<|V| forces some component with fewer edges than vertices, hence a tree component; apply (3.1) to that component instead (one sentence).
